NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday marked 25 years of continuous leadership in government, with leaders from across the world extending congratulations and highlighting bilateral ties with India.Belgian prime minister Bart De Wever congratulated PM Modi on completing 25 years in government, from his tenure as Gujarat chief minister to his leadership in New Delhi.De Wever also recalled his recent visit to India and said he looked forward to further strengthening the partnership between the two countries.Dominican prime minister Roosevelt Skerrit described PM Modi as a “dear friend” and congratulated him on 25 years of continuous service as head of government.Skerrit praised PM Modi’s friendship with Dominica and the support extended to its people, saying he looked forward to further strengthening ties between the two countries.Nigerian president Bola Ahmed Tinubu congratulated PM Modi on what he called a “truly historic milestone”, noting that October 7 marked 25 years since Modi first assumed office in 2001 as Gujarat chief minister.Tinubu described 25 years of uninterrupted leadership as a rare achievement in a democracy and said it reflected the confidence placed in Modi by the Indian people.He credited PM Modi’s leadership with driving development in areas including infrastructure, digital public goods, financial inclusion and innovation, saying these efforts had lifted millions and inspired countries across the Global South.Tinubu also highlighted the India-Nigeria strategic partnership, recalling PM Modi’s state visit to Abuja in November 2024, when Nigeria conferred on him the Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger, one of the country’s highest national honours.Calling India and Nigeria fellow democracies and leading voices of the Global South, Tinubu said both countries shared a commitment to a fairer, more inclusive and representative international order.He wished PM Modi good health, strength and continued success in serving the people of India.Bhutanese prime minister Tshering Tobgay published a tribute titled “Modi's leadership reflects wisdom, courage, empathy”, recalling his interactions with Modi and praising his journey from Gujarat to the national stage.Tobgay highlighted Modi’s vision of a developed India by 2047 and India’s assistance to Bhutan, while also pointing to the close bilateral relationship under the “B4B” (Bharat for Bhutan, Bhutan for Bharat) framework. He also recalled PM Modi being conferred Bhutan’s highest honour, the Order of the Druk Gyalpo.Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi extended her congratulations to PM Modi, praising his long political career and contribution to the development of Indian society and the country.Takaichi also recalled her visit to India in July and discussions with PM Modi on taking the Japan-India Special Strategic and Global Partnership to a new stage.She noted that 2027 will mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Japan and India and said the two countries would further strengthen cooperation towards a “Free and Open Indo-Pacific”.PM Modi marked the milestone on October 7, 25 years after he first took oath as Gujarat chief minister in 2001. He served as chief minister until May 2014, before becoming prime minister in May 2014.
Article Summary: PM Modi marked the milestone on October 7, 25 years after he first took oath as Gujarat chief minister in 2001. Leaders from across the world congratulated PM Modi on completing 25 years in government. Belgian prime minister Bart De Wever said he looked forward to further strengthening the partnership between the two countries.

Article Title: Delhi HC seeks Centre's response on body cameras on cops during protests
Article Text:
Delhi HC asks Centre to consider mandatory body cameras for police

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has asked the Centre to consider a PIL seeking mandatory use of body-worn cameras by police during protests and crowd-control operations, saying the issue should not be treated as a “grey area” requiring court intervention.The court asked the Centre to take a decision on the plea within six months.A bench headed by Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambhre said any direction on the use of body-worn cameras would have wider implications for policing and could not be confined to the Delhi Police alone.The bench observed while hearing the plea, “Why should we direct them to legislate? It cannot be said that it is a grey area.”The court questioned the need for judicial intervention when existing laws already provide for regulation of police procedures in areas covered by the legislature.The PIL, filed by Chahat Raghav, seeks directions for the mandatory use of body-worn cameras by Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed during protests and crowd-control operations. It also seeks a comprehensive framework governing the storage, retention, integrity and evidentiary use of footage recorded by the cameras.The petitioner has cited the use of body-worn cameras by traffic police and a tender issued for their procurement, arguing that the technology is already available to the authorities.Senior Advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that body-worn cameras could enhance transparency and accountability during protests, especially in cases involving allegations of police excesses and counter-allegations against protesters.Sibal said the cameras were already being used by police in some situations, but only sporadically. He argued that the Delhi Police's 2022 standing order on rallies and demonstrations did not specifically provide for body-worn cameras and that a clear protocol was needed.He also disputed that the existing videography mechanism was sufficient, saying the recording under the standing order was different from footage captured by cameras worn directly by police personnel involved in crowd control.Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the respondents, submitted that the Delhi High Court's PIL rules require a petitioner to first approach the concerned authorities through a representation. He said the present petition could be treated as such a representation.Sharma also submitted that the Supreme Court, while hearing a matter concerning protests at Jantar Mantar, had directed the authorities to frame an SOP and that the existing mechanism already provides for videography of protests. The court recorded the ASG's statement and directed the respondents to communicate their decision on framing an SOP for the use of body-worn cameras within six months.The petitioner was given liberty to approach the High Court again in case of any inaction.The move comes amid heightened security in the New Delhi, Central Delhi and North Delhi districts following a series of demonstrations against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed in large numbers, with multilayered barricades placed at several points to prevent protesters from entering restricted areas.
Article Summary: The Delhi High Court has asked the Centre to consider a PIL seeking mandatory use of body-worn cameras by police during protests and crowd-control operations. The move comes amid heightened security in the New Delhi, Central Delhi and North Delhi districts following a series of demonstrations against the Election Commission.

Article Title: Who is Vivek Bhagat?: What is the controversy around the Delhi Police officer
Article Text:

Who is Vivek Bhagat?

What are the allegations against him?

Why is his promotion controversial?

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police officer ACP Vivek Bhagat, currently posted as sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) in Connaught Place, has come under scrutiny after three women journalists alleged sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The complaints were transferred to the Delhi Police Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial” enquiry. Bhagat has since consented to keeping his current duty charge as additional deputy commissioner of police on hold pending the enquiry.Bhagat is a Delhi Police officer currently serving as SDPO, Connaught Place. He was among 12 Selection Grade DANIPS officers assigned the current duty charge of Additional DCP in an order approved by Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu.The Delhi government later modified the order after Bhagat formally requested that the charge concerning him be kept on hold, citing the pending Crime Branch enquiry.Bhagat had also been involved in police action during protests in June, when he was injured amid clashes between protesters and police.During those protests Bhagat said that he was allegedly surrounded and overpowered during the clashes and was beaten, kicked and punched.He reported alleged head injuries, bruises and broken teeth.An ANI report from the time said Bhagat was injured by stone and bottle pelting near Tolstoy Marg. The injuries were sustained while police were dealing with protesters during the June clashes.Three women journalists complained of sexual harassment following a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 3.One journalist specifically alleged that Bhagat sexually assaulted her while she was covering the protest. She said she had approached him after noticing that no women police personnel were present while protesters were being detained.According to her complaint, she asked Bhagat about the absence of women personnel, following which he allegedly sexually assaulted and pushed her.The allegations have not been established. The Delhi Police transferred the complaints to its Crime Branch, which is examining the allegations and recording statements of the complainants and other people concerned.The allegations emerged just days before Bhagat was among 12 officers assigned the current duty charge of Additional DCP.A senior police officer said the promotions were routine and that the request for the promotions had been sent much earlier.After the allegations and the pending enquiry came to light, Bhagat wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner saying he consented to keeping the order concerning him on hold until the enquiry was dealt with.The Delhi government subsequently modified the administrative order, putting his Additional DCP charge on hold.The Crime Branch enquiry will determine the facts surrounding the allegations. The complaints remain allegations at this stage, and the material available does not establish that Bhagat committed sexual harassment.The Press Council of India has meanwhile expressed “shock and dismay” over the allegations and urged Delhi Police to act on the journalists’ complaints, saying journalists must be able to work without facing aggression or threats.
Article Summary: Vivek Bhagat is a Delhi Police officer currently serving as SDPO, Connaught Place. Three women journalists complained of sexual harassment following a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 3. The Delhi Police transferred the complaints to its Crime Branch, which is examining the allegations and recording statements.

Article Title: Anant Ambani unites over 50 animal welfare groups under Vantara's ‘Champions of Care’ initiative
Article Text:
"Every day, there are countless people who quietly care for animals in need, often with limited resources and little recognition, but with immense compassion,"

"Their work reminds us that kindness has no boundaries and that every life deserves care, protection and dignity. Through Champions of Care, we hope to stand alongside this work, strengthen the care available to community animals and help build a more compassionate India.

For us, this is what Every Life Matters truly means."

"I deeply appreciate Shri Anant Ambani Ji’s vision and leadership in bringing Champions of Care to life,"

"I have travelled across the world, but have rarely seen an animal care centre where such advanced facilities and technology have been made available for animals, with a level of care comparable to what we aspire to provide for people.

What touched me most was his personal effort to listen to the organisations, understand their challenges on the ground and respond with practical and sustainable solutions. By bringing these organisations together, he is not only recognising their dedication but also strengthening their collective ability to care for animals.

This is a meaningful step towards a more compassionate future for community animals across India."

A national framework for grassroots animal care

Sustainable infrastructure and nationwide collaboration

On World Animal Day, Anant Ambani, Executive Director at Reliance Industries Limited, announced 'Champions of Care', a new national initiative designed to strengthen community animal welfare through practical, sustainable solutions.Convened at Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat, the landmark gathering brought together more than 50 animal welfare organisations from across India, alongside key statutory advisory members, establishing a collaborative framework to elevate animal care standards nationwide.The initiative addresses the critical needs of community animals, including street dogs, cats, abandoned livestock, and working animals such as horses and donkeys. Through targeted support in veterinary care, rescue operations, shelter facilities, and responsible population management programmes, the nationwide network is estimated to reach and support around two million animals every year.At the heart of the movement is the simple recognition that every community animal deserves care, protection, and dignity. Speaking on the launch of the initiative, Anant Ambani highlighted the unsung dedication of grassroots caregivers who work tirelessly across the country.Anant Ambani said.Eight members of the Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) participated in the event. S. P. Gupta, former Chairman and current member of the AWBI, commended the vision and leadership behind the nationwide drive.Gupta noted.The two-day gathering in Jamnagar provided participating delegates with an immersive experience of advanced animal care standards. Representatives toured Vantara's specialised facilities for rescued elephants and big cats, as well as naturalistic environments housing free-roaming species such as bison, zebras, and antelopes. The experience demonstrated how excellence in veterinary medicine, nutrition, housing, and lifelong care can be applied to elevate community animal welfare.Beyond facility tours, the gathering focused on connection, dialogue, and collaborative problem-solving among non-governmental organisations. A key milestone was the signing of a Letter of Understanding between Vantara and all participating organisations, formalising a shared commitment to strengthen community animal welfare. The understanding establishes a framework for knowledge sharing, capacity building, and practical support shaped by ground-level needs.Towards the close of the gathering, each participating organisation was presented with a Certificate of Appreciation signed by Anant Ambani, acknowledging their tireless devotion to animal protection.Rather than relying on short-term assistance, the initiative focuses on long-term organisational capacity and resilience. Vantara will support diverse needs identified by partner groups, including mobile veterinary services, ambulances, rescue tools, and diagnostic and treatment equipment.To help shelters become more self-sustaining and efficient, support will cover sustainable infrastructure upgrades such as solar power systems, rainwater harvesting, and improved drainage systems. Partner organisations also plan to roll out education programmes for youth, alongside quarantine and disease management infrastructure to combat infectious diseases.Conceived as an extension of Vantara's commitment to Every Life Matters, Champions of Care will continue expanding its network in the coming years, creating a connected, unified response to animal welfare across India.
Article Summary: Champions of Care is a national initiative designed to strengthen community animal welfare through practical, sustainable solutions. The initiative addresses the critical needs of community animals, including street dogs, cats, abandoned livestock, and working animals such as horses and donkeys. The nationwide network is estimated to reach and support around two million animals every year.

Article Title: How will economy be impacted if India-US trade deal doesn’t happen? RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra answers
Article Text:
Malhotra’s comments come within days of FM Sitharaman indicating discussions having "reached a plateau”.

Where India-US trade deal talks stand

India’s trade agreements with other countries should help mitigate the impact of possible US tariffs if a trade deal does not come through, indicated RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra on Wednesday.Asked about the possible impact on the economy if the India-US trade deal is not finalised, Malhotra said, “The impact depends on what extent tariffs are going to be applied. So it's premature to answer. But obviously, it will have some negative impact.”“At the same time, we have had a number of trade agreements now in the recent past. Some of them have been operationalized, others are in the pipeline. They will help. The industry at the same time has diversified its exports,” Malhotra said at the post monetary policy press conference.“So all these things will mitigate the effect in case there is an additional tariff on some of the sectors,” he added.Also Read | Will Russian oil be economically viable for India if Trump tariffs return? Malhotra’s comments come within days of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman indicating that the India-US bilateral trade agreement remains deadlocked, with discussions having "reached a plateau”.Sitharaman’s remarks came a few days after US Trade Representative (USTR) Jaimeson Greer indicated that an agreement was not close."I don't think there's something imminent, but we truly have identified the universe of items that are sticking points. We're working diligently toward them," he said after his meeting with Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Trump also discussed bilateral trade during a phone conversation last week, along with defence, energy and other matters.Meanwhile, Sitharaman said, “The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it," she said at the Munich Security Conference.Also Read | ‘Rate cuts off the table’: Why RBI hiked repo rate by 25 basis points but also raised GDP growth forecast to 7.1% Sitharaman said the US would look to narrow its trade deficit with India, which stood at an estimated $34 billion last year, down from $41 billion in 2024-25. The gap could reduce further as India has increased its purchases of energy from the US.Officials from India and the US have continued negotiations on the trade agreement and have repeatedly indicated that the talks were close to being concluded. The US has been pushing for greater access for its agricultural products in India through lower tariffs. However, the recent law permitting duties of up to 100% on imports of Russian oil is viewed as another hurdle in the negotiations.An agreement, in any case, can be finalised only after the Indian government has clarity on the extent of additional tariffs that could be imposed on its exports. At present, the USTR has imposed an additional duty of 10-12.5% on more than 50 countries, citing their alleged failure to prevent imports of goods produced using forced labour. The US is also examining structural overcapacity in countries including India, a charge that India has denied.In February, India and the US had agreed on a bilateral trade agreement under which the Trump administration imposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. However, the arrangement was put on hold after the Supreme Court ruled that the “reciprocal tariffs” were illegal.
Article Summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said India's trade agreements with other countries should help mitigate the impact of possible US tariffs if a trade deal does not come through. His comments come within days of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman indicating that the India-US bilateral trade agreement remains deadlocked.

Article Title: 'Like your movie, money is Ata Pata Laapata': SC directs Rajpal to pay Rs 2 crore by Oct 13
Article Text:
'Money is Ata Pata Laapata': SC directs Rajpal to pay Rs 2 crore by Oct 13

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed actor Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore towards the amount due to the complainant in a cheque-bounce case by October 13, saying it would consider his plea against the High Court order after the payment is made.Yadav, who was present in court, brought a demand draft of Rs 1.15 crore, while the remaining Rs 85 lakh is to be paid by October 13 through a buyer of his property, who was also present in court.The court, however, came down heavily on Yadav's conduct and warned that it could enhance his sentence, saying repeated extensions were being granted only to ensure that the complainant received the money.The Court said the deposit was directed to secure the amount due to the complainant and observed that Yadav’s conduct had not satisfied it.“Law should not be utilised like this”, the Court said.After passing the order, the bench had an informal exchange with Yadav, who spoke about the financial difficulties caused by his film Ata Pata Laapata. He said the film had resulted in losses of around Rs 200-250 crore and that the producers had also suffered losses.During the hearing, the Court also remarked in jest that the film's title was synonymous with Yadav's conduct.“Like your movie, your money is also Ata Pata Laapata, gayab”, the CJI said.Before the order was passed, film actor Rajpal Yadav appeared before the Supreme Court for the hearing of a cheque-bounce case against him and said, "The matter is before the honourable Supreme Court, and our legal team and lawyers will speak on the issue. I have the utmost respect for my country and for the Supreme Court. Whatever decision is taken by the court, wherever and whenever it is delivered, will be universally accepted. "Yadav later greeted the bench, saying, “Pranam karta hoon,” and spoke about the losses of Rs 200-250 crore he had incurred over the film.The CJI advised him to make a good film and entertain people, adding in jest that advocates appearing before the Supreme Court were also good actors and could be cast in his films.Yadav's counsel told the Court that he had approached the Registry to make the payment, but RTGS was not permissible. He said the actor had therefore brought a demand draft of Rs 1.15 crore.On the remaining Rs 85 lakh, the counsel said a buyer of Yadav's property was present in court and the amount would be paid once the transaction was completed.Yadav submitted that the dispute arose from a Rs 5 crore liability connected with the film Ata Pata Laapata, while the film had caused much larger losses.The case arises from an alleged loan extended to Yadav by Murli Projects Pvt Ltd in 2010 for Ata Pata Laapata. Seven repayment cheques of Rs 1.05 crore each were subsequently dishonoured.
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders actor Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore towards the amount due to the complainant in a cheque-bounce case by October 13. Yadav, who was present in court, brought a demand draft of Rs 1.15 crore. The remaining Rs 85 lakh is to be paid by a buyer of his property. The court warned that it could enhance his sentence.

Article Title: Government set to halt sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses diversion for ethanol
Article Text:
File photo: Sugarcane at a market, in Guwahati

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (ESY) starting November, amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season and indications of a further decline in output due to drought in major sugarcane-growing states of Maharashtra and Karnataka.TOI has learnt that government will notify the decision soon, ahead of the start of the new ESY. While ethanol supply year runs from Nov 1 to Oct 31, sugar season in India runs from Oct 1 to Sep 30. Government specifies the quantity of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses that can be diverted for ethanol production to meet the mandatory blending target for the green fuel in petrol.The move comes at a time when domestic sugar supplies remain tight. Mills diverted about 30 lakh tonnes of sugar, or around 10% of total output, for ethanol production during the sugar season that ended on September 30. The new sugar season began on October 1 with opening stocks of around 37.5 lakh tonnes, compared with nearly 50 lakh tonnes a year ago.Industry sources said there was no scope for allowing further diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol, as ensuring adequate domestic sugar supplies remains a priority for both govt and mills.With the possibility of a fall in output in the current season, particularly in Maharashtra and Karnataka, government would prioritise sugar availability over additional diversion for ethanol.Disallowing the use of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol in 2026-27 would enable mills to produce more sugar from the available cane, helping augment domestic supplies and meeting consumption requirements.Government has said that the share of sugar diverted for ethanol has declined from around 12% in 2022-23 to around 9% in 2025-26. Besides, nearly three-fourths of ethanol produced in the country now comes from grains, particularly maize, reducing the dependence on sugar-based feedstock.“Meeting the demand for 20% ethanol blending in petrol won’t be an issue. With indications of millers getting a better price, it won’t be a problem for them either. Government would have to continue with the ban on exports and may have to allow more imports as well,” an industry analyst said.Sugar production in the 2025-26 season was hit by crop diseases, waterlogging and adverse weather in key producing states. Against the initial production estimate of around 343 lakh tonnes, output was estimated at around 306 lakh tonnes in August, including the quantity diverted for ethanol production.After accounting for the diversion to ethanol, net sugar production in 2025-26 was around 279 lakh tonnes, barely enough to meet the normative domestic consumption requirement of 280-285 lakh tonnes.
Article Summary: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (ESY) The move comes amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season. Mills diverted about 30 lakh tonnes of sugar, or around 10% of total output, for ethanol during the sugar season that ended on September 30.

Article Title: 'Inflation man Modi's reign of terror continues': Congress on repo rate hike
Article Text:
Congress slams Centre after RBI raises repo rate to 5.5%

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Wednesday attacked the Centre after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, saying the move would further increase the financial burden on the public.Calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi “inflation man”, the Congress said, “Inflation Man Modi's reign of terror continues. Now the public's back will be broken even further.”The party said the rate hike would push up borrowing costs for home, car, personal and business loans, resulting in higher EMIs and potentially longer repayment periods. “To curb inflation as per Modi's intent, the RBI has today raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%,” it said."This means your home loan, car loan, personal loan, and business loan interest rates will now increase. Now you'll have to pay higher EMIs, and the loan repayment period will also get extended. The promise was of 'good days,' but what we got were days of extortion," he added.The RBI's monetary policy committee unanimously approved the hike and shifted its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening, citing stronger-than-expected economic growth and broader price pressures.The rate increase would raise the monthly EMI on a Rs 1 crore home loan with a 15-year tenure by around Rs 1,500, assuming a base rate of 8.50%. If borrowers keep their EMI unchanged, the higher interest rate could extend the repayment period by roughly six instalments.The RBI also raised its FY27 real GDP growth forecast by 40 basis points to 7.1%, while increasing its inflation projection by 20 basis points to 5.2%. RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said stronger capacity utilisation, bank credit growth, government capital expenditure and infrastructure spending were supporting investment and demand.CPI inflation rose to 4.8% in August from 4.5% in July. Malhotra said price pressures had broadened beyond volatile items, with food inflation becoming more widespread, including higher sugar and onion prices.The Congress said the government's promise of “good days” had instead delivered “days of extortion”.
Article Summary: The Congress attacked the Centre after the Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. The party said the rate hike would push up borrowing costs for home, car, personal and business loans. The Congress said the government's promise of “good days” had instead delivered “days of extortion”

Article Title: ED summons Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann kin in 5 crore graft case
Article Text:
File photo: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann

NEW DELHI: The alleged Rs 5 crore bribery allegation against Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann 's wife Gurpreet Kaur has taken a new turn with ED summoning his brother-in-law Amardeep Singh Grewal for questioning in the case.Grewal, a prominent Punjabi film personality, was asked by ED to appear before it Wednesday, sources said, adding he sought an adjournment. ED issued a second summons for Friday for him to appear for recording his statements.Kaur had earlier denied the allegation against her and sent a legal notice to ex-Punjab and Haryana HC judge Ranjit Singh for claiming she had demanded Rs 5 crore to suppress a rape case.Grewal's summoning comes a day after the high court ordered a CBI investigation against Mann's OSD in another bribery allegation.ED is probing Grewal's links to the alleged bribery deal and the role of his East Sunshine Production Pvt Ltd.The overseas transactions of the company are also being trailed to verify any bribery or alleged money laundering accusations.
Article Summary: Amardeep Singh Grewal, a prominent Punjabi film personality, was asked by ED to appear before it Wednesday. He sought an adjournment. ED issued a second summons for Friday for him to appear for recording his statements. Kaur had earlier denied the allegation against her.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Enforcement Directorate has unearthed a bribery racket involving top executives of at least 40 public sector undertakings and government banks, besides some corporate houses engaged in siphoning off and laundering hundreds of crores of corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds channelled through multiple charities promoted by a class XII dropout, who has been caught impersonating as a medical doctor for close to three decades.According to ED, the fake doctor, Dharmendra Kumar Chandradev, received CSR donations in his multiple trusts registered for the purpose of laundering money meant for charity and exempted from taxation. These funds were further returned back to the "donor" in cash, after retaining his commission. The racket involved some corporate houses, hospitals, public sector companies and govt banks. Top executives of these PSUs were heavily bribed for releasing CSR funds.On Oct 1, the central agency carried out searches at eight locations across Maharashtra, Bengal, Gujarat and Delhi-NCR related to these bogus donations cases. The agency seized several pieces of evidence and details of transactions related to PSU executives and corporate hospitals, in addition to Rs 21 lakh in unaccounted cash."The CSR mechanism was utilised as a conduit for conversion of accounted funds into unaccounted cash.Funds amounting to Rs 200 crore have been routed through the above mechanism," ED has estimated through its preliminary investigation.The agency further said its probe revealed that CSR contributions from corporate houses were "returned substantially in cash" to the contributors after deduction of a small commission.Searches have also revealed a network of agents and intermediaries who channelled CSR funds to the trusts, which were thereafter routed through shell entities controlled by market operators. Most of these entities have also been flagged in multiple GST fraud investigations."At least 40 PSUs and public sector banks across the country have provided CSR donations to the trusts operated by the accused. Several projects were only partially executed or not executed in proportion to the funds received, while vendor bills were inflated and excess funds routed through bogus or shell entities. Kickbacks and commissions were allegedly paid to intermediaries facilitating the CSR funding," ED said.
Article Summary: The racket involved some corporate houses, hospitals, public sector companies and govt banks. Top executives of these PSUs were heavily bribed for releasing CSR funds. On Oct 1, the central agency carried out searches at eight locations across Maharashtra, Bengal, Gujarat and Delhi-NCR.

Article Title: Cabinet okays new body to bring roads, rail, ports, aviation under one planning framework

NEW DELHI: The Cabinet on Tuesday approved setting up India’s first integrated transport and logistics authority, giving the new body a mandate to plan, appraise and monitor projects worth over Rs 500 crore across roads, railways, ports, aviation, waterways, urban mobility and logistics.The Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) is aimed at ending fragmented planning across multiple transport ministries and agencies and driving greater coordination and multi-modal integration in infrastructure development. Announcing the decision, I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, “By fostering greater coordination and multi-modal integration, ITLA is a new institution responsible for prospective planning for infrastructure development in the country. ”The new agency is modelled on similar institutions in the US, UK, Germany, Australia and Japan, and was first reported by TOI in April 2024.Govt said ITLA will also create a unified transport data repository by obtaining relevant transport and logistics datasets from multiple sources, including GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS-based systems, urban traffic management systems and other databases. It will undertake data analytics for planning, monitoring and impact assessment.Each transport and logistics-related ministry will have an ITLA division to ensure better coordination and implementation of projects and schemes, officials said.The agency will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more. It will also evaluate five-year sectoral plans and annual plans of transport ministries to ensure consistency with the master plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.Vaishnaw said ITLA will coordinate the resolution of inter-ministerial issues and assess the impact of projects after their completion, making post-completion assessment an important part of its mandate.
Article Summary: The Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) is aimed at ending fragmented planning across multiple transport ministries and agencies. The new body will plan, appraise and monitor projects worth over Rs 500 crore across roads, railways, ports, aviation, waterways, urban mobility and logistics. The agency will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more.

Dehradun (Uttarakhand) [India], October 6 (ANI): Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami participated in a programme organised at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan at the Chief Minister's Camp Office on Tuesday to mark Uttarakhand becoming a fully literate state.On the occasion, the Chief Minister felicitated neo-literates who successfully cleared the examination conducted by the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS).The Chief Minister said the achievement was the result of the hard work and collective participation of teachers, students, neo-literates, volunteers and everyone associated with the campaign while congratulating the people of Uttarakhand on the state becoming the sixth fully literate state in the country.He said achieving the goal of full literacy in Uttarakhand, with its challenging geographical terrain and remote areas, reflected the strong determination and collective strength of the people of the state.The Chief Minister said Uttarakhand had achieved the distinction of becoming a fully literate state under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the ULLAS-Nav Bharat Saaksharta Programme."After Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim, Uttarakhand has become the sixth fully literate state in the country," he said.He said the achievement would further strengthen the state's resolve to emerge as a leader in education and other sectors.Congratulating the neo-literates, the Chief Minister said they had demonstrated that there is no age limit for learning and that it is never too late to move forward."Education not only instils confidence in individuals but also opens up new opportunities in their lives," he said.He said literacy is no longer limited to reading, writing or signing one's name. "In the changing times, awareness of rights and duties, digital and financial literacy, and life skills are also important components of literacy."The Chief Minister said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, continuous efforts are being made to make education more inclusive and modern across the country. He said that the Prime Minister's vision is to ensure that no person remains deprived of education and an educated person not only transforms their own life but also contributes significantly to the progress of their family, society and nation.He said the state government was focusing on improving the quality of education as well as the overall development of students."Under the Nanda Gaura Yojana, eligible girl students are being provided financial assistance. Virtual classrooms and a central studio are being established in 500 schools across the state to ensure that students in remote areas also have access to quality education. As many as 189 Atal Utkrisht Schools are being operated in the state. Under the Mukhyamantri Balashray Yojana, free education is being ensured for orphaned children. Work is also underway to develop modern laboratories in 100 schools each at the high school and intermediate levels," CM Dhami said.The Chief Minister said the achievement of full literacy should not be viewed as a destination but as a new beginning."The focus must now be on taking digital literacy, financial literacy, health awareness and life skills to every citizen. Continuous efforts will be made to ensure that every citizen of the state keeps pace with changing technology and is able to use it to improve their quality of life," he said.Education Minister Dhan Singh Rawat said Uttarakhand had achieved the significant milestone of becoming a fully literate state under the leadership of Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami. He said around 25,000 volunteers had made an important contribution to the success of the campaign."The state has now set a target of achieving 100 per cent literacy over the next six months".He said the National Education Policy 2020 has set a national target of increasing the Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education to 50 per cent by 2035, and Uttarakhand is moving rapidly towards achieving this target this year itself.The Education Minister said the state government was committed to ensuring access to education for every child. He added that no school would be closed in a village as long as even a single child in that village is enrolled as a student. (ANI)

NEW DELHI: Jack Dorsey’s Bluetooth-based messaging app Bitchat has been removed from Indian app stores following government intervention, putting the spotlight on concerns over decentralised communication. Government sources quoted by news agency PTI said on Tuesday that the app posed a law-and-order concern and therefore had to be taken down.The sources told PTI that Bitchat allows users to send messages through multiple Bluetooth “hops” without relying on conventional internet connectivity, raising concerns that it could be used to bypass restrictions imposed by authorities.“The government is duty-bound to maintain law and order,” sources said, adding that the app's ability to facilitate communication through Bluetooth was a concern.On proposals to restrict minors' access to social media, government sources said there was no such proposal under consideration. They pointed to Australia's experience, saying restrictions had not prevented children from accessing social media without accounts.The government is instead consulting industry representatives and experts, including those with expertise in psychology, sources said.“We have to find a better solution...when the right solution comes, we will bring it in front of you,” the sources said, stressing that a solution needed to be found.Apple removed Bitchat from the India App Store following a demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Dorsey said in an X post on Saturday.“Government of India officially removes Bitchat from the App Store,” Dorsey wrote, sharing a screenshot of Apple's App Review notice.The notice said the removal was “per demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)” because the app “includes content that is illegal in India”. It cited Section 69(A) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, under which the takedown demand was issued.Google has also removed the app from the Play Store in India, while Apple said it remained available in other territories selected by the developer. Its TestFlight version would also no longer be available for testing in India.Bitchat had previously faced government action in July. The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) had then directed GitHub to restrict access to its repositories, citing concerns that the decentralised network could enable communication during internet restrictions and make lawful detection more difficult.
Article Summary: Apple removed Bitchat from the India App Store following a demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) Google has also removed the app from the Play Store in India, while Apple said it remained available in other territories selected by the developer. Government sources said the app posed a law-and-order concern and therefore had to be taken down.

Article Title: The India mood: The country is going places. Will my career follow?
Article Text:
AI generated image for representational purpose

High on confidence about India, not so much about jobs

Jobs top the worry list

People most worried about unemployment

Education is second in the list of worries

What the government data show

The classroom-to-career gap

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A sense of collective pride, and yet a feeling of individual disquiet. This is probably the most accurate description of the mood among India's more connected, urban-skewed population. There is confidence in the larger macroeconomic story, even as there is lingering uncertainty about the jobs market and an apparent weakening of the old assumption that education is a sure-shot route to upward mobility. Ipsos's September surveys capture that dilemma between hope and anxiety. India ranks first among 30 markets on consumer confidence but 16th on jobs, and unemployment is the issue Indian respondents worry about most.India's consumers are upbeat about the economy. In Ipsos's September 2026 Global Consumer Confidence Index, India scores 66.9, the highest among the 30 markets, compared with a global average of 48.4. Ipsos says its India sample is more urban, educated and/or affluent than the general population and hence the results should be read as reflecting the views of a more "connected" segment.India's Current Index, an indicator of how people rate present conditions, is 70.7, and its Investment Index is 73.2, both the highest among the 30 markets in the published survey.Its Expectations Index, at 66.4, ranks fourth, so respondents are also buoyant about the future.The contrast is particularly sharp against the world's major advanced economies. Among the G7, the US has the highest overall consumer-confidence score at 50.5, followed by Great Britain at 48.2 and Canada at 47.3. Italy scores 43.0, Germany 41.4, France 40.6 and Japan 39.4. India, at 66.9, is therefore 16.4 points above the best-performing G7 economy.Across the countries surveyed, India is the most confident market, followed by Sweden at 60.0 and Malaysia at 54.8. At the other end, Türkiye is lowest at 35.3, followed by Argentina at 37.8 and Japan at 39.4. The gap between India and Türkiye is more than 31 points. Only one number breaks the pattern. India's Jobs Index is 59.3, putting it in 16th spot. On current conditions and investment, India sits more than 30 points above the 30-country average. On jobs, its lead is just 1.6 points.In the September edition of Ipsos's What Worries the World survey, 47% of Indian respondents name unemployment among the three issues they find most worrying in the country, making it the most frequently cited concern in India. The global average is 29%. South Africa, Argentina, Singapore, Indonesia and Chile are the only countries with a higher share of respondents citing unemployment as a worry.Among the G7, unemployment is cited as a top concern by 28% in Canada and Italy, 20% in the US, 19% in Great Britain, 16% in France and 13% each in Germany and Japan, well below India's 47%. Across the 30 countries surveyed, concern is highest in South Africa, at 69%, and lowest in the Netherlands, at 6%.The same survey also finds strong optimism among Indian respondents. Seventy per cent say the country is heading in the right direction, against a global average of 38%. Only Singapore, at 80%, records a higher figure. Meanwhile, 79% describe the current economic situation in India as good, again compared with a global average of 38%.Here too India stands apart from the G7. The share saying their country is heading in the right direction is 44% in Canada, 36% in Japan, 28% in Great Britain, 27% in the US, 23% in Italy, 14% in Germany and 11% in France. Singapore does best on this measure at 80%, while France is at the bottom at 11%.The jobs concern, in other words, does not stem from general economic pessimism. The more connected Indians Ipsos surveys can be positive about the economy and still name unemployment as one of the country's most worrying problems.Ipsos switched its India consumer-confidence sample from a mixed methodology to online-only in April 2026, a break that the September report flags. Long-term comparisons therefore need caution.Do the official numbers help explain this contrasting mood?Real GDP grew 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter of 2026-27, according to MoSPI estimates. Private final consumption expenditure, the broad measure of household consumption, increased 7.1%, while gross fixed capital formation rose 11.9% at constant prices. Those numbers are broadly consistent with Ipsos's strong readings for current conditions and investment sentiment.The labour market data are more mixed. The government's monthly Periodic Labour Force Survey put India's unemployment rate for people aged 15 and above at 5.0% in August on the Current Weekly Status measure, marginally lower than 5.1% in July. But the improvement came from rural India. Rural unemployment fell from 4.5% to 4.1%, while the urban rate was almost unchanged, moving from 6.7% to 6.8%. The urban Worker Population Ratio was also 47.0%, unchanged from July and below 47.5% a year earlier.These figures are not directly comparable with Ipsos's Jobs Index. PLFS measures actual labour-market status; Ipsos measures perceptions of job security and the employment environment. There is another limitation to headline unemployment numbers. NITI Aayog has also highlighted job quality, informality and underemployment as labour-market concerns, dimensions that an unemployment rate alone cannot fully capture.Taken together, the data help explain how the seemingly contradictory findings can coexist.Education is India's second-most cited concern, at 36%. That is the highest among the 30 countries, against a global country average of 13%. India's top two concerns, unemployment and education, are both closely tied to economic opportunity. The government's labour survey tracks one measure that spans both. In the latest PLFS annual report, covering 2025, 25.0% of people aged 15-29 were not in employment, education or training, or NEET . Among those aged 15-24, the share was 21.0%.The same report put the unemployment rate at 9.9% for 15-29-year-olds, 13.6% for urban youth and 6.5% for people with at least secondary education. NEET is not an unemployment measure: it also includes young people who are neither working nor studying but may not be looking for work. So for Indians, confidence in the economy, current conditions and investment is higher than in any other market. The Jobs Index is the exception, and the official data point to where some of the strain lies: among urban youth and the educated.That is the lived reality the surveys capture. The pride is collective: it is about where the country is heading. The disquiet surfaces when the conversation turns to jobs and education. With technology rapidly changing the nature of work, continuous learning and reskilling are becoming an economic necessity. But many workers and young people still lack the support, guidance and pathways needed to navigate that transition.The surveys offer a snapshot of that churn.
Article Summary: India ranks first among 30 markets on consumer confidence but 16th on jobs. 47% of Indian respondents name unemployment among the three issues they find most worrying in the country. South Africa, Argentina, Singapore, Indonesia and Chile are only countries with a higher share of respondents citing unemployment as a worry.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.
