Article Title: Oil prices hover near $100 as Middle East supply holds up, Gulf risks persist
Article Text:
Houthi attacks keep Gulf supply risks alive

Supply squeeze could last

Demand recovery may take longer

Oil prices remained close to $100 a barrel on Tuesday, with steady Middle Eastern oil exports helping to ease supply concerns. However, continued attacks in the region kept traders alert to the risk of disruptions to Gulf supplies.Brent crude was trading at $100.6 a barrel, up 24 cents or 0.24%, while WTI stood at $89.60, gaining 17 cents or 0.19%.The benchmarks have eased from around $103 a barrel after shipping data showed Middle Eastern crude exports had exceeded pre-war levels on four days in the final week of September. Oil shipments held up despite attacks on vessels travelling through the Strait of Hormuz.The supply picture also improved after G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves. The group also pledged not to restrict energy exports following pressure from US President Donald Trump.But the stronger oil flows have not removed concerns about future supplies, with fresh attacks adding to uncertainty over Gulf shipments.Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said on Monday that they had attacked several sites in Saudi Arabia, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh and Abha airport.Saudi Arabia had not immediately confirmed the attacks.The attacks came as US-Iran talks remained at a stalemate, while the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi forces continued to raise concerns about possible disruptions to supplies from Saudi Arabia, the region's largest oil exporter."Without a clear diplomatic breakthrough or a further material improvement in export efficiency, the floor under prices looks reasonably firm," Waterer said.The concerns around supply could persist well beyond the immediate crisis. Oil industry executives at a conference in London on Monday said shipping bottlenecks, deep cuts in refinery output and inventory withdrawals that could take years to replace could keep global oil prices high beyond this year.The Strait of Hormuz has been a major source of disruption since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran at the end of February, when Iran effectively closed the waterway and choked exports through the crucial shipping route.The disruption has been compounded by attacks on oil and gas infrastructure, which have hampered production and affected exports of crude oil and refined fuels."I think it is going to be bedlam for the bulk of the end of the year and maybe 2027," Petronas CEO Tengku Muhammad Taufik said.Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser said it could take up to two years to rebuild global oil stockpiles that have been drawn down as an emergency measure.Speaking at the Energy Intelligence Forum in London in his first conference address since the start of the Iran war, Nasser said the scale of the stockpile withdrawals would make replenishment a long process."Until Hormuz fully re-opens and confidence returns, the crude reality is that pressure at both ends of the barrel will intensify. Even then, replenishing inventories while meeting demand could take up to two years," he said.Nasser said 3 billion barrels had been lost since the start of the conflict, while 1 billion barrels had been withdrawn from global inventories. The reference to both ends of the barrel covers unrefined crude as well as refined products such as diesel and jet fuel.The supply disruption could also affect the timeline for a recovery in global oil demand.ConocoPhillips Executive Chair Ryan Lance said demand could take until 2028 or 2029 to recover from this year's decline, although he expects it to grow after that.Lance said the floor for US benchmark WTI crude would rise to around $70 a barrel, with a mid-cycle price of $65 to $70 a barrel.US oil production could exceed 14 million to 14.5 million barrels per day if prices remain strong, he said, although he did not specify what he meant by strong prices.Brent futures had traded just above $100 a barrel on Monday, while WTI was close to $90, keeping both benchmarks elevated as traders balanced stronger Middle Eastern exports against the continuing risk of supply disruptions.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $100.6 a barrel, up 24 cents or 0.24%, while WTI stood at $89.60. The benchmarks have eased from around $103 a barrel after shipping data showed Middle Eastern crude exports had exceeded pre-war levels on four days in the final week of September.

Article Title: First India-born cheetahs with Botswana lineage: Kuno welcomes 5 cubs, India's total count now 60
Article Text:
Five cubs were born at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh, increasing India's cheetah population to 60.





BHOPAL: Project Cheetah crossed another milestone on Sunday with the birth of five cubs at MP's Kuno National Park, taking India's total cheetah count to 60, including 41 born in the country.The cubs were born to 32-month-old cheetah KJ, making her the third India-born female to give birth in the country after Mukhi and KGP12, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav announced in a social media post, describing it as "an important milestone in the emergence of the next generation of India's cheetah population".The development is an important marker in the progress of Project Cheetah, which aims not only to establish a viable population of the feline in India 70 years after it was declared extinct, but also to enable the species to breed and sustain itself over successive generations, say officials.The birth has an added genetic significance. The father of the five cubs is a male brought from Botswana, making them the first India-born cheetahs to carry the Botswanan lineage. This adds a new genetic lineage to the growing cheetah population in the country.The latest births also reveal a shift in Project Cheetah from the initial phase of relocation from Africa to India to establishing a self-sustaining population through breeding on Indian soil, say officials.Both Yadav and MP chief minister Mohan Yadav congratulated the veterinarians, forest officials, field staff, park management and others associated with Project Cheetah.KJ and her litter will be closely monitored in the coming days, officials said, adding that the initial period is considered critical for newborn cheetahs because cub mortality can be high in the wild.Another generation born on Indian soil adds another chapter to the country's cheetah reintroduction programme, which began with the arrival of the first batch of cheetahs from Namibia in Sept 2022 and subsequently from South Africa.
Article Summary: Five cubs born at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh, increasing India's cheetah population to 60. Father of the five cubs is a male brought from Botswana, making them the first India-born cheetahs to carry the Botswanan lineage.

Article Title: Ghee, refined oil in her bag: Woman ‘caught stealing’ at Noida DLF Mall, video emerges
Article Text:
At DLF Mall of India in Noida, security apprehended a woman during a bag inspection





NOIDA: A video showing a woman being escorted out of a store at DLF Mall of India in Sector 18 after she was allegedly accused of stealing ghee and refined cooking oil has gone viral on social media. Police and the mall management, however, have not confirmed that the woman stole any items and said she had paid for the products.The video, which is around 30 seconds long, shows two female security guards stopping a woman inside the store and taking her away. The woman can be seen covering her face as she walks out of the premises. During the incident, a store employee can be heard accusing her of stealing goods.Several claims accompanying the video on social media allege that the woman had been visiting the store for around a month and had allegedly taken ghee and refined oil on multiple occasions without paying. Some posts also claim that her activities had been captured on the store’s CCTV cameras.However, no CCTV footage supporting these allegations has been shared along with the viral video. The video itself also does not show the woman stealing any item or leaving the store without making a payment.Following the circulation of the video, information was sought from Sector 20 police. Police said their preliminary inquiry found that the woman had paid for the items she had taken from the store.The mall management also conveyed the same information to the police, officials said.“The woman had paid for the items. The allegations being made on social media have not been established,” police said.The video has triggered a range of reactions on social media, with several users sharing and commenting on the incident. It has reportedly been shared by more than 100 people.Police said the footage currently establishes only that the woman was stopped by security personnel and that a store employee accused her of theft. The circumstances in which the woman was stopped and what transpired inside the store cannot be conclusively determined from the viral video alone.Officials said claims made on social media should not be treated as established facts unless supported by evidence. Police also said that neither the mall nor the store management has submitted a formal complaint regarding theft in connection with the incident so far.Police are examining the available information and other aspects of the incident. Further details will be established if additional evidence, including CCTV footage or statements from those involved, becomes available.
Article Summary: A video showing a woman being escorted out of a store at DLF Mall of India in Noida has gone viral on social media. The video shows two female security guards stopping a woman inside the store and taking her away. During the incident, a store employee can be heard accusing her of stealing goods.

Article Title: Delhi-NCR traffic alert: Central Delhi barricaded amid INDIA bloc march, VIP movement; avoid these routes
Article Text:
Commuters on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza in Mayur Vihar also reported heavy congestion. (Photo credit: X)

Connaught Place, Old Delhi see heavy congestion

Delhi-Noida corridor also hit

VIP movements add to Delhi's recurring traffic problem

Why is traffic restricted today?





NEW DELHI: Traffic snarls hit several parts of Delhi-NCR on Tuesday as restrictions for the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission added to congestion in central Delhi, while commuters on other key stretches reported heavy traffic and prolonged delays.The INDIA bloc MPs marched from the Parliament House complex towards the Election Commission headquarters to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Delhi Traffic Police had put special arrangements in place from 8am, regulating or diverting traffic around Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, Parliament Street, Jantar Mantar Road, Ashoka Road and adjoining stretches.Commuters were advised to avoid unnecessary travel through the affected areas and expect barricading, diversions and congestion.Heavy traffic was also reported on the Ring Road near AIIMS-Safdarjung Hospital, in and around Connaught Place, on Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg in Old Delhi and on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza, Mayur Vihar.The traffic police separately responded to complaints of prolonged congestion in and around Connaught Place, saying personnel had been deployed at critical junctions and were carrying out active traffic regulation and decongestion measures.On Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg in Old Delhi, the traffic police said movement was slow because of prevailing traffic arrangements and high traffic volume. Personnel were deployed at key points to regulate traffic and ease the congestion.On Ring Road near AIIMS-Safdarjung Hospital, the traffic police said it had alerted the concerned traffic circle for immediate deployment and active regulation at critical junctions, merging points and bottlenecks.It also said special attention was being given to ensuring the unhindered movement of ambulances and emergency vehicles.Commuters on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza in Mayur Vihar also reported heavy congestion.Responding to a commuter's complaint on X, the Delhi Traffic Police said personnel were actively regulating movement and had been deployed at critical merging points and bottlenecks to ensure smoother traffic flow.The traffic police also responded to complaints about congestion around Krishna Menon Marg, Kartavya Path and adjoining roads, saying restrictions were being imposed only when required for operational or security reasons and for the minimum possible duration.The traffic disruption comes a day after the movement of Swiss President Guy Parmelin to Rajghat led to road restrictions and lengthy delays for commuters in central Delhi.During Parmelin's Rajghat visit on Monday, commuters reported being stuck for extended periods around ITO and other key stretches.A recent VIP movement involving Russian President Vladimir Putin had, however, shown that traffic could keep moving despite security restrictions, with congestion clearing relatively quickly.The issue has raised questions over whether better advance planning, deployment and communication can reduce the impact of such movements on daily commuters.The immediate trigger in central Delhi was the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. The opposition has accused the poll panel of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls and has been demanding Kumar's resignation.The protest came a day after the Supreme Court refused to pass an interim order suspending Kumar, while issuing notices to the Centre, the Election Commission and Kumar over allegations concerning decision-making during the SIR process.The court said it would examine whether statutory requirements had been followed.The INDIA bloc's wider campaign includes further protests and programmes against the SIR exercise.For commuters, however, the immediate concern remained the same: long diversions, slow-moving traffic and delays across some of the city's busiest roads.
Article Summary: Heavy traffic reported on Ring Road near AIIMS-Safdarjung Hospital, in and around Connaught Place, on Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg in Old Delhi. Commuters on the Delhi-Noida corridor near Crowne Plaza in Mayur Vihar also reported heavy congestion. Traffic disruption comes a day after the movement of Swiss President Guy Parmelin to Rajghat led to road restrictions.

Article Title: Video: Staffer washes utensils in toilet at Korba sweet shop; food dept issues notice
Article Text:
A video showing utensils being washed on a toilet floor at New Delhi Sweets raised significant concerns





RAIPUR: A video showing utensils being washed on a toilet floor at New Delhi Sweets in Korba’s Niharika area has prompted a food safety inspection and an improvement notice, with officials warning of licence suspension if hygiene deficiencies are not addressed within three days.The footage, recorded by a customer and circulated on social media, showed employees washing utensils inside the toilet.Food safety officer Sangharsh Kumar Mishra inspected the outlet following the video’s circulation.During the inspection, the operator attributed the practice to a disruption in water supply, claiming utensils were washed there as an emergency measure.Mishra described the practice as unhygienic and a violation of food safety norms. The establishment was directed to improve its arrangements within two to three days or face suspension of its food licence.

Article Title: 2 workers injured, 500 evacuated after massive fire guts labour camp outside Lucknow airport; watch
Article Text:
Fire broke out at an impermanent housing facility near Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport in Lucknow

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the primary focus after an incident like this? Improving safety protocols Providing better worker support and compensation Investigating the cause thoroughly Raising awareness among workers 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





LUCKNOW: At least two workers were injured while evacuating a three-storey makeshift labour camp after a major fire engulfed the structure outside Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport on Tuesday morning.The blaze broke out around 6.50am at the Tata Projects labour colony, about 800 metres from the airport. The PVC-panel structure housed workers engaged in ongoing airport development projects. Thick smoke and flames were visible from several kilometres away, triggering panic in the area.The injured workers were identified as Nirmal, 30, son of Mukhiya, a resident of Saharsa in Bihar, and Rahul Kumar, 26, son of Bhagwati Din Pal, a resident of Salipur in Pratapgarh. Both were taken for medical attention. The Fire Department said neither had sustained burn injuries.The camp had 33 rooms, with 11 on each floor, and could accommodate around 500 workers deployed in round-the-clock shifts. The fire spread rapidly through the combustible panels and engulfed the structure within minutes. Officials did not specify how many workers were present when the fire broke out.The Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting team immediately dispatched a Domestic Fire Tender to the site, while a Crash Fire Tender from the airport and fire tenders from the Uttar Pradesh Fire Service were also deployed.All workers were evacuated safely, officials said.A newly introduced 22,000-litre water bowser was among the fire tenders deployed by the UP Fire Service headquarters. Firefighters climbed to the first and second floors to tackle the flames from close quarters. Two LPG cylinders exploded during the operation, increasing the risk to the firefighting teams.The blaze was brought under control in about 45 minutes and was prevented from spreading to nearby areas. Chief Fire Officer Ankush Mittal reached the site and supervised the operation.An inspection later indicated that the fire started in Barrack 9 while food was being prepared. The temporary structure was completely damaged.“Initial findings shared by Tata Projects indicate that the fire started while some labourers were preparing food using LPG cylinders. The company provides meals for its workers, and the use of flammable materials or unauthorised cooking arrangements within the labour colony is prohibited. Workers had been repeatedly instructed to follow these safety guidelines," said an official source.Following the incident, Tata Projects shifted all affected workers to newly arranged barracks and shelters as a precautionary measure.
Article Summary: Blaze broke out around 6.50am at the Tata Projects labour colony. The PVC-panel structure housed workers engaged in ongoing airport development projects. The injured workers were identified as Nirmal, 30, and Rahul Kumar, 26. Both were taken for medical attention.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion. It plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses.

Article Title: RBI rate hikes ahead? BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027
Article Text:
BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could raise interest rates by 100 basis points through the first half of 2027, according to Bank of America (BofA) Securities. The brokerage has also moved up its estimate for the first rate hike, now expecting the hike in October instead of December.BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.The new forecast is twice the size of BofA's earlier 50 basis point estimate.“Our bigger forecast shift is arguably the quantum of hikes, as we are raising our total quantum of hikes from 50bp earlier, to 100bp now,” BofA said.BofA expects the RBI to raise rates by 50 basis points in the fourth quarter of 2026 and another 50 basis points in the first half of 2027. It also expects the central bank to change its monetary policy stance in December.“The RBI will switch the stance in December to one of calibrated tightening”, the report said.So, what has changed in BofA's view? The brokerage said the domestic economy remains resilient, giving the RBI less reason to wait before raising rates.At the same time, inflation risks are becoming broader.Oil prices remained around $100-110 per barrel for most of September, BofA said. It also pointed to rising risks of fuel price increases and food-related supply pressures.Strong economic growth is another factor behind the revised outlook. BofA said the strength of the economy is reducing the need for the RBI to keep monetary conditions accommodative.Non-food credit growth stood at 17.8 per cent year-on-year in September, while investment demand is expected to remain healthy in the second quarter of FY27.Inflation pressures are also spreading, according to the report. BofA said food inflation is becoming more broad-based, while wholesale inflation is increasingly spreading to other sectors. Tradables inflation rose to 5.9 per cent in August 2026.The brokerage has also laid out a scenario in which the RBI could go beyond the 100-basis-point increase it currently expects. If real GDP growth stays around 7 per cent and headline inflation remains close to 5.5 per cent, BofA said the central bank could raise rates by more than 100 basis points.In that case, front-end rates could rise above 6.5 per cent, the brokerage said.But a sharp slowdown in growth could change the rate outlook. BofA said the RBI could deliver fewer hikes or no hike if growth falls below 7 per cent and moves towards 6 per cent on a forward-looking basis.
Article Summary: Bank of America Securities sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027. BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.

Article Title: 90% of dementia cases in TN go undiagnosed: State turns focus to early screening and care
Article Text:
About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia (AI Image)





CHENNAI: With more than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed, the state is looking at making the condition a “public health priority”.“Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. The number of people with dementia is projected to double to 10 lakh,” says Ramani Sundaram of Dementia India Alliance (DIA), which recently organised DemCon in Chennai, a conference on the condition.DIA is a national organisation focused on dementia awareness, care, support and brain healthAt DemCon, state health minister K G Arunraj said the govt would work towards a “coordinated state plan”. “The MoU between the department of health and family welfare and DIA is an important step in this direction,” said Arun Raj. “This partnership is an expression of our shared commitment to strengthening dementia care.”The state plan will look at standardising screening, assessment, referral and treatment, as well as making diagnosis, systematic referrals and follow-up part of the existing primary healthcare infrastructure.“It’s important to create awareness as dementia care costs about Rs 3 lakh per person annually, apart from the informal cost of care provided by family members,” says Ramani. “Cognitive impairment cannot be reduced to simply asking an elderly person whether they are becoming forgetful. ”An ongoing screening programme conducted since Feb by DIA in collaboration with the state govt among 2,500 elderly people in Coimbatore, Erode and Chengalpet, found 9% had cognitive impairment.Among those screened, 30% reported neurological problems such as slowness, tremors, falls or limb weakness, while 28% had sleep disturbances. About 27% reported feeling sad, irritable, or disinterested in their usual activities, while 18% had trouble with memory, wayfinding or planning. About 12% had difficulty speaking, understanding, naming, reading or writing, and 7% said they heard voices or saw images when alone.About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia. “There was substance abuse in about 15% of those screened, while a large percentage – 42 – chewed tobacco. These are also among the risk factors. Up to 45% of dementia can be prevented if these are addressed. So, this is an important part of the action plan to make Tamil Nadu a dementia-aware state,” says Ramani.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. More than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed. The state is looking at making the condition a ‘public health priority’

These passengers had arrived at IGI Airport on Sept 25 from Hong Kong via Vietnam.During Customs proceedings, the passengers were subjected to a baggage search, which resulted in the recovery of 10 autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 11 remote controllers of autel robotics mdx-1 drones, 10 adaptors, 10 USB chargers, 20 data cables, 40 remote controller joysticks and other parts. Article Title: In 2021, Elon Musk put up $100 million for carbon removal; five years later, 136 teams have removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂ and raised $3.3 billion
Article Text:
Elon Musk 's $100m carbon-removal challenge

136 teams removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂

The challenge helped attract $3.3bn in capital

875 patents filed during the competition

Mati Carbon won the $50m grand prize

In 2021, the Musk Foundation put up $100 million for a global competition aimed at finding ways to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and oceans and store it durably. The XPRIZE Carbon Removal competition ran for four years, drew 1,334 registered teams from more than 88 countries and helped turn carbon removal into a credible, investable sector. According to XPRIZE's Post-Prize Impact Report, released in April 2026, the 136 Distinguished Teams collectively removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂ over the course of the competition, and participating companies raised more than $3.3 billion in capital during and after the prize period. The report also points to hundreds of companies created, thousands of skilled jobs generated and 875 patents filed.XPRIZE announced the $100 million competition on February 8, 2021, with funding from Elon Musk and the Musk Foundation. It officially launched on Earth Day, April 22, 2021, when team registration opened. The challenge asked teams worldwide to develop technologies that remove CO₂ from the atmosphere or oceans and store it durably and sustainably, while showing a credible path to gigatonne-scale removal.The competition ran through Earth Week 2025, and XPRIZE describes it as the largest incentive competition in history. Teams worked across four removal pathways: air, rocks, ocean and land.According to the impact report, the 136 Distinguished Teams collectively removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂ over the course of the competition. They also sold 9,475,438 tonnes of carbon credits, a figure that includes future deliveries of tonnes removed. Buyers included Microsoft, Google, Salesforce, Stripe, Shopify, Meta, McKinsey, BCG and JPMorgan.The two figures measure different things. The 243,552 tonnes were actually removed during the competition, while the larger credit figure also counts tonnes sold for delivery in the future.The removal total remains small against the problem it targets. Global CO₂ emissions run at roughly 37 billion tonnes a year, so the tonnes removed during the competition amount to far less than 0.001% of one year's emissions. XPRIZE's argument is that the competition built a pipeline of demonstrated solutions that can now move from pilots towards commercial deployment. It also acknowledges that carbon markets face headwinds in 2026.Participating companies raised more than $3.3 billion in capital during and following the prize period, which XPRIZE describes as a 33-fold return relative to the $100 million purse. The money is capital raised by the companies themselves, not money returned to Musk or the XPRIZE Foundation, and XPRIZE's report does not specify which participating companies the figure covers.XPRIZE says the competition's structured milestones and third-party validation led to a 464% increase in average deal size and a 176% increase in the number of unique investors backing competing teams. More than half of the 1,334 registered teams were founded after the prize launched, and dozens are now running pilot projects or commercial deployments across six continents.Teams filed 875 patents during the four-year prize period from 2021 to 2025, which XPRIZE says is a 958% increase in the annual rate of patent filings. XPRIZE also estimates that the $100 million purse helped catalyse more than $300 million in research and development that might not otherwise have happened.The technologies ranged from engineered systems that capture carbon directly from air or oceans to approaches that use natural processes involving rocks, soil and organic waste.XPRIZE announced the winners on April 23, 2025, selecting them from 20 finalists across 11 countries. Each winning team removed more than 1,000 net tonnes of CO₂ in the competition's final year.The $50 million grand prize went to Mati Carbon, which spreads finely crushed basalt on agricultural land in India to accelerate a natural weathering process that permanently removes atmospheric CO₂. XPRIZE says the approach also benefits smallholder farmers through improved soil health, reduced agricultural inputs and increased income.NetZero, a French biochar company operating in Brazil, received $15 million as first runner-up. Vaulted Deep, a US waste-management company that stores unusable organic waste deep underground, received $8 million. UNDO Carbon, which uses enhanced rock weathering in Scotland and Canada, received $5 million. XFACTOR awards of $1 million each went to Planetary, for ocean alkalinity enhancement, and Project Hajar, a partnership between Aircapture and 44.01 that captures CO₂ from the air and mineralises it underground in the United Arab Emirates. Across the competition, $5 million also went to student teams and $15 million to milestone awards for early-stage demonstrations.With the competition over, XPRIZE says the field has moved beyond technical validation and early demonstrations towards commercial readiness. The next test is whether stronger demand for carbon removal emerges to scale these technologies to the level scientists say will be needed.
Article Summary: The XPRIZE Carbon Removal competition drew 1,334 registered teams from more than 88 countries. 136 Distinguished Teams collectively removed 243,552 tonnes of CO₂ over the course of the competition. participating companies raised more than $3.3 billion in capital during and following the prize period.

Article Title: TP-Link Systems Inc issues public statement; says: Stop calling us a 'Chinese company', we are an American company and no threat to …
Article Text:
TP-Link Systems Inc issues public statement; says: Stop calling us a 'Chinese company'

Here’s what TP-Link said

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier recently filed a civil lawsuit against Wi-Fi router manufacturer TP-Link. The lawsuit accuses the company of misleading Florida consumers about its products’ security and its ties to China. In the 59-page lawsuit, Uthmeier said that Chinese state-sponsored hackers exploited TP-Link routers sitting in American living rooms. “Many of those models cannot update themselves automatically, and TP-Link has stopped supporting them”. “They also told Floridians they had split from China and that they build U.S. products in Vietnam. That is fiction. Research and manufacturing remain rooted in China. Less than 1% of the parts in that Vietnam plant actually come from Vietnam,” he further added.TP-Link has now responded to the lawsuit, issuing an official statement saying that it is a US company, and not a ‘Chinese’ firm. “TP-Link Systems is a U.S. company that complies with U.S. privacy and data protection laws,” the company said adding “Any claims that our products present a threat to user security or grant unauthorized network access to foreign governments are baseles”.In a press release, Steve Kovsky, corporate affairs officer for TP-Link Systems Inc.said “The coordinated lawsuits are built on false premises. They do nothing to advance national security while unfairly penalizing an industry-leading U.S. company”.“We stand fully behind the security of our products, the integrity of our company and our people, and our commitment to serving the best interests of our customers in the United States and globally. We look forward to refuting these baseless allegations in court,” Kovsky added.In the release, the company further stated”: “For months, California-based TP-Link Systems has provided state regulators with clear, verifiable documentation demonstrating two fundamental facts: TP-Link Systems devices sold in the U.S. are manufactured in Vietnam and TP-Link Systems is an independent, U.S. company that is not owned or controlled by any foreign government.”“Any claims that our products present a threat to user security or grant unauthorized network access to foreign governments are baseless. TP-Link Systems is a U.S. company that complies with U.S. privacy and data protection laws. We perform comprehensive security testing and rely on trusted third-party security labs for additional scrutiny to ensure our products meet the highest security standards and are recognized as among the most secure on the market. We meet or exceed all industry best practices for monitoring and preventing vulnerabilities and actively support our customers to mitigate any issues that occur as they are identified. We do not, and will not, share customer network data with foreign governments or unauthorized third parties”.
Article Summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier recently filed a civil lawsuit against Wi-Fi router manufacturer TP-Link. The lawsuit accuses the company of misleading Florida consumers about its products’ security and its ties to China. In a press release, Steve Kovsky, corporate affairs officer for TP- Link Systems Inc. said “The coordinated lawsuits are built on false premises”
